newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-HSBC takes over Brazil's Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-HSBC takes over Brazil's Bamerindus.

text.p: Hong Kong & Shanghai Banking Corp will take over failed Banco Bamerindus under a deal announced Wednesday by the Central Bank, ending months of speculation over the fate of Brazil's fourth largest bank.
Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said HSBC will be allowed to assume Bamerindus' selected assets and liabilities and turn it into a new bank with an immediate $1.0 billion capital injection.
The new bank, which Central Bank officials said is likely to be called HSBC-Bamerindus, will assume and honor all Bamerindus international obligations and credit.
HSBC's takeover of Bamerindus will involve 5.7 billion reais in Central Bank's credit lines, of which 2.5 billion reais from the government's PROER program to finance bank mergers and acquisitions.

Bamerindus, which since early last year had been plagued by rumors it would be sold due to its widely known liquidity troubles, is considered the last of Brazil's large private banks that needed restructuring.
In 1995, the Central Bank brokered a similar deal allowing the takeover of the healthy portion of failed bank Banco Nacional by private bank Unibanco.
And early last year, the Central Bank announced the acquisition of failed Banco Economico by Excel Banco. Economico and Nacional were among Brazil's top 10 financial institutions.
Like most Brazilian banks, Bamerindus suffered from the effects of the Real stabilization plan, which slashed inflation and virtually eliminated banks' high profits earned on wide arbitrage spreads.
Bamerindus' investment in the pulp and paper sector with the creation of its subsidiary Inpacel, which drowned in debts, was also seen as one of the bank's biggest headaches.

A solution for Bamerindus had been delayed for months on the insistence of controlling majority shareholder Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira, a powerful senator and government ally, that he remain in charge.

With the takeover deal, Andrade Vieira's assets will be frozen as required by law until what was left of Bamerindus and remained in Central Bank's hands is liquidated or when all of the old bank's liabilities are paid off.
